sanskrit.deva:
अथ हैनं कौसल्यश्चाश्वलायनः पप्रच्छ ।
भगवन्कुत एष प्राणो जायते ।
कथमायात्यस्मिन्शरीरे ।
आत्मानं वा प्रविभज्य कथं प्रातिष्ठते ।
केनोत्क्रमते ।
कथं बाह्यमभिधत्ते ।
कथमध्यात्ममिति ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
atha hainaṃ kausalyaś cāśvalāyanaḥ papraccha |
bhagavan kuta eṣa prāṇo jāyate |
katham āyāty asmin śarīre |
ātmānaṃ vā pravibhajya kathaṃ prātiṣṭhate |
kenotkramate |
kathaṃ bāhyam abhidhatte |
katham adhyātmam iti || 1 ||

padaccheda.iast: atha ha enam kausalyaḥ ca āśvalāyanaḥ papraccha bhagavan kutaḥ eṣaḥ prāṇaḥ jāyate katham āyāti asmin śarīre ātmānam vā pravibhajya katham prātiṣṭhate kena utkramate katham bāhyam abhidhatte katham adhyātmam iti
padaccheda.deva: अथ ह एनम् कौसल्यः च आश्वलायनः पप्रच्छ भगवन् कुतः एषः प्राणः जायते कथम् आयाति अस्मिन् शरीरे आत्मानम् वा प्रविभज्य कथम् प्रातिष्ठते केन उत्क्रमते कथम् बाह्यम् अभिधत्ते कथम् अध्यात्मम् इति

translations.text: Then Kausalya Āśvalāyana asked him: ‘Venerable sir, from where is this prāṇa born? How does it come into this body? How does it abide, dividing itself? By what does it go out? How does it support what is outside, and how what is within the body?’

notes: Śaṅkara: though the greatness of prāṇa has been found by the breaths, who have ascertained what it is, yet, being a composite, it may be an effect; so I ask from what cause it is born. ‘How does it come into this body’: what is the occasion of its taking a body? Having entered, how does it abide, making a division of itself? By what particular function does it go out of this body? bāhyam: what concerns beings and what concerns the gods. abhidhatte: supports; ‘supports’ is to be supplied with ‘what is within the body’ also.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्मै स होवाच ।
अतिप्रश्नान्पृच्छसि ।
ब्रह्मिष्ठोऽसीति ।
तस्मात्तेऽहं ब्रवीमि ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmai sa hovāca |
atipraśnān pṛcchasi |
brahmiṣṭho 'sīti |
tasmāt te 'haṃ bravīmi || 2 ||

padaccheda.iast: tasmai saḥ ha uvāca atipraśnān pṛcchasi brahmiṣṭhaḥ asi iti tasmāt te aham bravīmi
padaccheda.deva: तस्मै सः ह उवाच अतिप्रश्नान् पृच्छसि ब्रह्मिष्ठः असि इति तस्मात् ते अहम् ब्रवीमि

translations.text: He said to him: ‘You ask questions beyond questions. You are a great knower of Brahman; therefore I tell you.’

notes: Śaṅkara: prāṇa itself, being hard to know, calls for a hard question; you ask even about its birth and the rest, so you ask questions beyond questions. You know Brahman in a high degree, so I am pleased; therefore I tell you what you have asked: listen.

sanskrit.deva:
आत्मन एष प्राणो जायते ।
यथैषा पुरुषे छायैतस्मिन्नेतदाततम् ।
मनोकृतेनायात्यस्मिञ्शरीरे ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ātmana eṣa prāṇo jāyate |
yathaiṣā puruṣe chāyaitasminn etadātatam |
manokṛtenāyāty asmiñ śarīre || 3 ||

padaccheda.iast: ātmanaḥ eṣaḥ prāṇaḥ jāyate yathā eṣā puruṣe chāyā etasmin etat ātatam manaḥ-kṛtena āyāti asmin śarīre
padaccheda.deva: आत्मनः एषः प्राणः जायते यथा एषा पुरुषे छाया एतस्मिन् एतत् आततम् मनः-कृतेन आयाति अस्मिन् शरीरे

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

words.meaning: by what the mind has done

translations.text: This prāṇa is born from the Self. As a shadow is cast by a man, so this (prāṇa) is spread upon that (Self). It comes into this body by what the mind has done.

notes: Śaṅkara: from the Self: from the supreme Puruṣa, the imperishable, the True. As in the world a shadow arises, as an effect, where there is a man with head, hands and the rest as its cause, so on this Brahman, the true Puruṣa, this principle called prāṇa, which stands in the place of the shadow and is unreal in form, is spread, is fixed.

Śaṅkara: manokṛtena: by the action that the mind's intention, desire and the like have brought about; so the text will say ‘by merit to a world of merit’ (3.7), and another scripture ‘attached, together with his action’ (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.6). By that it comes into this body.

sanskrit.deva:
यथा सम्राडेवाधिकृतान्विनियुङ्क्ते ।
एतान्ग्रामानेतान्ग्रामानधितिष्ठस्वेति ।
एवमेवैष प्राण इतरान्प्राणान्पृथक्पृथगेव संनिधत्ते ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yathā samrāḍ evādhikṛtān viniyuṅkte |
etān grāmān etān grāmān adhitiṣṭhasveti |
evam evaiṣa prāṇa itarān prāṇān pṛthak pṛthag eva saṃnidhatte || 4 ||

lines.iast: evam evaiṣa prāṇa itarān prāṇān pṛthak pṛthag eva saṃnidhatte

padaccheda.iast: yathā samrāṭ eva adhikṛtān viniyuṅkte etān grāmān etān grāmān adhitiṣṭhasva iti evam eva eṣaḥ prāṇaḥ itarān prāṇān pṛthak pṛthak eva saṃnidhatte
padaccheda.deva: यथा सम्राट् एव अधिकृतान् विनियुङ्क्ते एतान् ग्रामान् एतान् ग्रामान् अधितिष्ठस्व इति एवम् एव एषः प्राणः इतरान् प्राणान् पृथक् पृथक् एव संनिधत्ते

grammar.en: past passive participle m. acc. pl.

translations.text: As a sovereign appoints his officers, saying ‘govern these villages, and you these’, so this prāṇa sets the other breaths each in its own place.

notes: Śaṅkara: as in the world a king, a sovereign, appoints officers over villages and the like, so this chief prāṇa appoints the other breaths, the eye and the rest, and the divisions of itself, each apart in its own place.

sanskrit.deva:
पायूपस्थेऽपानम् ।
चक्षुःश्रोत्रे मुखनासिकाभ्यां प्राणः स्वयं प्रतिष्ठते ।
मध्ये तु समानः ।
एष ह्येतद्धुतमन्नं समं नयति ।
तस्मादेताः सप्तार्चिषो भवन्ति ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
pāyūpasthe 'pānam |
cakṣuḥśrotre mukhanāsikābhyāṃ prāṇaḥ svayaṃ pratiṣṭhate |
madhye tu samānaḥ |
eṣa hy etad dhutam annaṃ samaṃ nayati |
tasmād etāḥ saptārciṣo bhavanti || 5 ||

lines.iast: eṣa hy etad dhutam annaṃ samaṃ nayati

padaccheda.iast: pāyu-upasthe apānam cakṣuḥ-śrotre mukha-nāsikābhyām prāṇaḥ svayam pratiṣṭhate madhye tu samānaḥ eṣaḥ hi etat hutam annam samam nayati tasmāt etāḥ sapta arciṣaḥ bhavanti
padaccheda.deva: पायु-उपस्थे अपानम् चक्षुः-श्रोत्रे मुख-नासिकाभ्याम् प्राणः स्वयम् प्रतिष्ठते मध्ये तु समानः एषः हि एतत् हुतम् अन्नम् समम् नयति तस्मात् एताः सप्त अर्चिषः भवन्ति

words.meaning: in the anus and the organ of generation
in the eye and the ear
from the mouth and the nose

grammar.en: past passive participle n. acc. sg.

translations.text: In the anus and the organ of generation (it places) the apāna. In the eye and the ear, going out through the mouth and the nose, prāṇa itself abides. In the middle is the samāna, for it carries evenly the food that is offered; from that arise these seven flames.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: here is the division.

Śaṅkara: in the anus and the organ of generation it places the apāna, a division of itself, which stays there removing urine, faeces and the like. In the eye and the ear, and going out by the mouth and the nose, prāṇa itself, which stands in the place of the sovereign, abides. In the middle, between the places of prāṇa and apāna, in the navel, is the samāna, so called because it carries evenly what is eaten and drunk.

Śaṅkara: since it carries evenly the food, eaten and drunk, that is thrown into the fire of the body, from that fire of the belly, whose fuel is what is eaten and drunk, when it has reached the region of the heart, these seven flames go out, in the head. The meaning is that the lighting up of form and the other objects, as seeing, hearing and the rest, comes about through prāṇa.

sanskrit.deva:
हृदि ह्येष आत्मा ।
अत्रैतदेकशतं नाडीनाम् ।
तासां शतं शतमेकैकस्याः ।
द्वासप्ततिर्द्वासप्ततिः प्रतिशाखानाडीसहस्राणि भवन्ति ।
आसु व्यानश्चरति ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
hṛdi hy eṣa ātmā |
atraitad ekaśataṃ nāḍīnām |
tāsāṃ śataṃ śatam ekaikasyāḥ |
dvāsaptatir dvāsaptatiḥ pratiśākhānāḍīsahasrāṇi bhavanti |
āsu vyānaś carati || 6 ||

padaccheda.iast: hṛdi hi eṣaḥ ātmā atra etat eka-śatam nāḍīnām tāsām śatam śatam ekaikasyāḥ dvāsaptatiḥ dvāsaptatiḥ pratiśākhā-nāḍī-sahasrāṇi bhavanti āsu vyānaḥ carati
padaccheda.deva: हृदि हि एषः आत्मा अत्र एतत् एक-शतम् नाडीनाम् तासाम् शतम् शतम् एकैकस्याः द्वासप्ततिः द्वासप्ततिः प्रतिशाखा-नाडी-सहस्राणि भवन्ति आसु व्यानः चरति

translations.text: This self is in the heart. Here are the hundred and one channels; each of them has a hundred (branches), and each of these seventy-two thousand branch channels. In these the vyāna moves.

notes: Śaṅkara: in the space of the heart, enclosed by the lotus-shaped lump of flesh, is this self: the subtle self, joined with the Self. In this heart are the chief channels, a hundred and one in number. Each chief channel has a hundred divisions, and each of these has seventy-two thousand branch channels. In these channels moves the air called vyāna, so named from pervading. As rays from the sun, it spreads from the heart through the channels that go everywhere and pervades the whole body. It is chiefly in the joints, the shoulders and the vital spots, and, arising between the working of prāṇa and of apāna, it does the deeds that need strength.

sanskrit.deva:
अथैकयोर्ध्व उदानः पुण्येन पुण्यं लोकं नयति ।
पापेन पापम् ।
उभाभ्यामेव मनुष्यलोकम् ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
athaikayordhva udānaḥ puṇyena puṇyaṃ lokaṃ nayati |
pāpena pāpam |
ubhābhyām eva manuṣyalokam || 7 ||

lines.iast: athaikayordhva udānaḥ puṇyena puṇyaṃ lokaṃ nayati
lines.deva: अथैकयोर्ध्व उदानः पुण्येन पुण्यं लोकं नयति

padaccheda.iast: atha ekayā ūrdhvaḥ udānaḥ puṇyena puṇyam lokam nayati pāpena pāpam ubhābhyām eva manuṣya-lokam
padaccheda.deva: अथ एकया ऊर्ध्वः उदानः पुण्येन पुण्यम् लोकम् नयति पापेन पापम् उभाभ्याम् एव मनुष्य-लोकम्

translations.text: Now by one of them the udāna, going upwards, leads by merit to a world of merit, by sin to a world of sin, and by both to the world of men.

notes: Śaṅkara: by the one among those hundred and one channels that goes upward, called suṣumnā, the air udāna, going upward and moving from the soles of the feet to the head, leads by meritorious action, that which scripture enjoins, to a world of merit, the place of the gods and the like; by sin, the opposite of that, to a world of sin, hell or birth as an animal and the like; and by merit and sin together, when they are equal, to the world of men: ‘leads’ carries on.

sanskrit.deva:
आदित्यो ह वै बाह्यः प्राण उदयति ।
एष ह्येनं चाक्षुषं प्राणमनुगृह्णानः ।
पृथिव्यां या देवता सैषा पुरुषस्यापानमवष्टभ्य ।
अन्तरा यदाकाशः स समानः ।
वायुर्व्यानः ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ādityo ha vai bāhyaḥ prāṇa udayati |
eṣa hy enaṃ cākṣuṣaṃ prāṇam anugṛhṇānaḥ |
pṛthivyāṃ yā devatā saiṣā puruṣasyāpānam avaṣṭabhya |
antarā yadākāśaḥ sa samānaḥ |
vāyur vyānaḥ || 8 ||

lines.iast: ādityo ha vai bāhyaḥ prāṇa udayati
lines.deva: आदित्यो ह वै बाह्यः प्राण उदयति

lines.iast: eṣa hy enaṃ cākṣuṣaṃ prāṇam anugṛhṇānaḥ
pṛthivyāṃ yā devatā saiṣā puruṣasyāpānam avaṣṭabhya

padaccheda.iast: ādityaḥ ha vai bāhyaḥ prāṇaḥ udayati eṣaḥ hi enam cākṣuṣam prāṇam anugṛhṇānaḥ pṛthivyām yā devatā sā eṣā puruṣasya apānam avaṣṭabhya antarā yat ākāśaḥ saḥ samānaḥ vāyuḥ vyānaḥ
padaccheda.deva: आदित्यः ह वै बाह्यः प्राणः उदयति एषः हि एनम् चाक्षुषम् प्राणम् अनुगृह्णानः पृथिव्याम् या देवता सा एषा पुरुषस्य अपानम् अवष्टभ्य अन्तरा यत् आकाशः सः समानः वायुः व्यानः

translations.text: The sun is the outer prāṇa; it rises, favouring this prāṇa in the eye. The deity that is in the earth (favours a man) by holding fast his apāna. The space between is the samāna; the air is the vyāna.

notes: Śaṅkara: the sun is the well-known outer prāṇa in the sphere of the gods. It rises, favouring with its light the prāṇa within the body that is in the eye: that is, giving the eye light for the perception of form. So too the well-known deity that presides over the earth holds fast a man's apāna, the working of the apāna: drawing it and mastering it, she favours it by pulling it downward. Otherwise the body would fall by its weight, or would fly up into open space.

Śaṅkara: the space between heaven and earth: the air that is in it is called space, as one says ‘the platforms (shout)’. It is the samāna, that is, it favours the samāna, because the samāna likewise stays in a space between. And the outer air in general is the vyāna, from the likeness of pervading: it favours the vyāna.

sanskrit.deva:
तेजो ह वा उदानः ।
तस्मादुपशान्ततेजाः ।
पुनर्भवमिन्द्रियैर्मनसि संपद्यमानैः ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tejo ha vā udānaḥ |
tasmād upaśāntatejāḥ |
punarbhavam indriyair manasi saṃpadyamānaiḥ || 9 ||

padaccheda.iast: tejaḥ ha vai udānaḥ tasmāt upaśānta-tejāḥ punarbhavam indriyaiḥ manasi saṃpadyamānaiḥ
padaccheda.deva: तेजः ह वै उदानः तस्मात् उपशान्त-तेजाः पुनर्भवम् इन्द्रियैः मनसि संपद्यमानैः

words.meaning: one whose heat has died down

translations.text: Fire is the udāna. Therefore one whose heat has died down (goes) to another birth, with the senses entering into the mind.

notes: Śaṅkara: the well-known outer fire in general is the udāna in the body: it favours the air udāna with its own light. Since the udāna, which brings about the going out, has heat for its nature and is favoured by the outer fire, when a man's natural heat has died down one should know that his life is spent and that he is about to die. He goes to another birth, another body, together with the senses, speech and the rest, as they enter into the mind.

sanskrit.deva:
यच्चित्तस्तेनैष प्राणमायाति ।
प्राणस्तेजसा युक्तः सहात्मना यथासंकल्पितं लोकं नयति ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yaccittas tenaiṣa prāṇam āyāti |
prāṇas tejasā yuktaḥ sahātmanā yathāsaṃkalpitaṃ lokaṃ nayati || 10 ||

lines.iast: prāṇas tejasā yuktaḥ sahātmanā yathāsaṃkalpitaṃ lokaṃ nayati
lines.deva: प्राणस्तेजसा युक्तः सहात्मना यथासंकल्पितं लोकं नयति

padaccheda.iast: yat-cittaḥ tena eṣaḥ prāṇam āyāti prāṇaḥ tejasā yuktaḥ saha ātmanā yathā-saṃkalpitam lokam nayati
padaccheda.deva: यत्-चित्तः तेन एषः प्राणम् आयाति प्राणः तेजसा युक्तः सह आत्मना यथा-संकल्पितम् लोकम् नयति

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: With whatever thought he has (at death), with that he comes to prāṇa. Prāṇa, joined with fire (the udāna), together with the self, leads him to the world he has intended.

notes: Śaṅkara: with whatever thought he has, with that thought, that intention, he comes, with the senses, to prāṇa, the working of the chief prāṇa: at the time of death, when the working of the senses has waned, he remains by the working of the chief prāṇa alone. Then his kinsmen say ‘he breathes, he lives’. That prāṇa, joined with fire, the working of the udāna, and together with the self, the owner, the enjoyer, leads that enjoyer, by the force of his deeds of merit and sin, to the world he has intended.

sanskrit.deva:
य एवं विद्वान्प्राणं वेद ।
न हास्य प्रजा हीयतेऽमृतो भवति ।
तदेष श्लोकः ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ya evaṃ vidvān prāṇaṃ veda |
na hāsya prajā hīyate 'mṛto bhavati |
tad eṣa ślokaḥ || 11 ||

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ evam vidvān prāṇam veda na ha asya prajā hīyate amṛtaḥ bhavati tat eṣaḥ ślokaḥ
padaccheda.deva: यः एवम् विद्वान् प्राणम् वेद न ह अस्य प्रजा हीयते अमृतः भवति तत् एषः श्लोकः

translations.text: He who, knowing thus, knows prāṇa: his line of offspring is not cut off, and he becomes immortal. On this there is this verse:

notes: Śaṅkara: whoever knows prāṇa as marked by its origin and the rest that have been told has this fruit, here and hereafter: his offspring, sons, grandsons and so on, are not cut off; and when the body has fallen, he becomes immortal through union with prāṇa. On this matter there is this verse, a mantra that states it in brief.

sanskrit.deva:
उत्पत्तिमायातिं स्थानं विभुत्वं चैव पञ्चधा ।
अध्यात्मं चैव प्राणस्य विज्ञायामृतमश्नुते विज्ञायामृतमश्नुत इति ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
utpattim āyātiṃ sthānaṃ vibhutvaṃ caiva pañcadhā |
adhyātmaṃ caiva prāṇasya vijñāyāmṛtam aśnute vijñāyāmṛtam aśnuta iti || 12 ||

lines.iast: utpattim āyātiṃ sthānaṃ vibhutvaṃ caiva pañcadhā
adhyātmaṃ caiva prāṇasya vijñāyāmṛtam aśnute vijñāyāmṛtam aśnuta iti
lines.deva: अध्यात्मं चैव प्राणस्य विज्ञायामृतमश्नुते विज्ञायामृतमश्नुत इति

padaccheda.iast: utpattim āyātim sthānam vibhutvam ca eva pañcadhā adhyātmam ca eva prāṇasya vijñāya amṛtam aśnute vijñāya amṛtam aśnute iti
padaccheda.deva: उत्पत्तिम् आयातिम् स्थानम् विभुत्वम् च एव पञ्चधा अध्यात्मम् च एव प्राणस्य विज्ञाय अमृतम् अश्नुते विज्ञाय अमृतम् अश्नुते इति

translations.text: Knowing the origin of prāṇa, its coming, its abiding, its fivefold lordship, and its state within the body, one attains immortality; knowing this, one attains immortality.

notes: Śaṅkara: its origin, from the supreme Self; its coming into this body, by what the mind has done; its abiding, in the anus, the organ of generation and the other places; its lordship, the fivefold placing of the divisions of its working, like a sovereign; its state outside, in the form of the sun and the rest, and within the body, in the form of the eye and the rest. Knowing prāṇa thus, one attains immortality. The words are said twice to mark the end of the matter of the question.
The mūla reads āyātiṃ; the bhāṣya in the same file has āyatim.
